title: AI Unboxing Video Maker for Online Sellers | AIVideosUGC
description: Create an AI unboxing video from one product photo: hands open the box, fold back the tissue, and reveal your item. Sized for TikTok and Shorts. Make yours now.
h1: Make an AI Unboxing Video of Your Product
lead: An AI unboxing video shows hands opening the box, folding back the tissue paper, and lifting your product into view. Add a photo, describe the packaging, and get a short reveal clip.
intro: Unboxing videos are about the moment the product comes out of the box. Viewers watch the lid come off, the tissue paper fold back, and the item get lifted into the light. It answers what a new customer wonders about: what arrives at the door, how it's packed, and what the product looks like once it's out.

Add a picture of the product, then describe the packaging in words, such as a matte black box with gold tissue or a kraft mailer with a card on top. Choose a 6, 10, 15, or 30 second reveal and frame it in 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4.

benefits.d: The opening seconds build anticipation: lid off, paper back, product up. That reveal is what keeps people watching.
There's no need to set up lights, a table, and a stack of packaging. Describe the box in a sentence instead.
If you already have a product photo, you can make a launch clip while inventory is still on its way.

steps.d: Use a clear shot of the item itself. The packaging comes from your description, so it doesn't need to be in the photo.

steps.t: Describe the box and the reveal
steps.d: Name the box color, material, and what's inside, for example “white box, pink tissue, a candle on top.” Choose vertical or square and the length.
Save the clip, or try a different box or wrapping in a new version to see which feels more like your brand.

uses.d: Post a vertical unboxing on launch day so followers see what arrives when they order.
A 15-second reveal fits Shorts and gives viewers a full look at the product once it's out.
Add the clip below your Shopify product photos to show what comes in the box.
Use a square version in Instagram or Facebook posts that show off gift-ready packaging.

faq.q: Do I need a photo of my packaging?
faq.a: No. Just use a product photo, then describe the box, wrapping, and any inserts in your sentence. The more specific you are about color and material, the closer the packaging gets to what you had in mind.

faq.q: Will my logo appear on the box?
faq.a: Don't count on it. Logos and printed words can come out slightly wrong in AI video, so describe the box by color and finish, then add your logo on top in CapCut. Requests that use logos or trademarks you don't own may be refused.

faq.q: What length works for an unboxing video?
faq.a: Ten seconds covers opening the box and showing the product. Choose 15 seconds for a slower reveal, 30 seconds for a full unboxing, or 6 seconds for a quick teaser.

faq.q: Can I make an unboxing video for a gift set or bundle?
faq.a: Yes. Upload a photo of the set and list what's inside, such as “three candles and a matchbox in a ribbon-tied box.” A few items usually come out cleaner than a crowded box.

overview.p: An unboxing clip is a short sequence: the container appears, a layer opens, and the product comes into view. The visual question is what arrives and how the reveal feels, so describe the materials and order instead of trying to fit the whole brand story into one shot.

overview.h2: Preview the experience before the shipment arrives
overview.p: A product photo can anchor the item while your description supplies the mailer, box, tissue, ribbon, card, or insert. Use the clip to plan a launch post or gift presentation, then compare the final packaging with the real stock before publishing.

input_guide.h2: Describe the layers people will open

items.d: Use a photo where the item or set is visible enough to recognize once it leaves the package.
Say whether the scene starts with a mailer, rigid box, drawer box, pouch, or another package shape.
Mention tissue, a sleeve, a ribbon, a card, or a paper insert in the order the hands should uncover them.
Matte, kraft, glossy, soft-touch, or colored materials give the packaging a visual identity without depending on tiny printed words.
For a bundle, name only the items that need to appear first so the box does not become visually crowded.

results.h2: A reveal built for a quick watch

items.d: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds for a teaser, standard reveal, or slower presentation.
Use 9:16 for vertical social posts, 1:1 for square feeds, or 16:9 for a wide product area.
The credit amount is visible before the job starts, and failed attempts release the reserved credits.
Review the package and item carefully, then use the file commercially with your own exact launch details added later.
A kraft mailer opens on a pale desk, white tissue folds back, and a ceramic mug is lifted by its handle.
A ribbon-tied cream box opens under warm light, revealing a small skincare set on a paper insert.
A printed-color box opens to three snack pouches arranged in a single layer with tissue around them.
A slim black box slides open to reveal headphones resting in a molded tray.
A deep green box opens beside pine branches, revealing two candles and a matchbox tied together.
A drawer-style package pulls open slowly and presents one watch against a dark foam insert.

after_download.h2: Make the reveal ready for a real launch

items.d: Type the product name, offer, date, and any insert wording in your editor rather than trusting generated lettering.
Compare the box color, tissue, included pieces, and order of opening with the package customers will actually receive.
If a channel asks you to label realistic AI content, enable its label before posting the reveal.

fit.h2: Packaging stories that fit this format
good: Giftable products with a clear box, wrap, or insert
Subscription boxes with a small, curated set
Product launches where the package is part of the first impression
Bundles that can be shown in one uncluttered reveal
not_ideal: Packaging whose value depends on perfectly readable small print
Large assortments that cannot fit into one clear opening sequence

examples.lead: Different boxes, different reveals. Pick the one closest to how your product really ships.
